technical_and_design_decisions: For U3, chaincode will be packaged as pre-built Docker images or compiled binaries, and the peer lifecycle will be updated to deploy these without requiring source code on the peer.

For U4, the VSCC will be enhanced to parse policy evaluation failures and output structured logs detailing the policy used, signer names, org names, and lacking signatures. This information will also be propagated to the SDK via event failure notifications.

For U6, the 'Certificate fingerprints hosted by organization' approach will be implemented, allowing endorsers to pull a certificate fingerprint list from a registered domain at endorsement time, integrated via an Auth Handler.

For U8, a new 'config_defaults' directory will be created, and existing YAML files (core.yaml, orderer.yaml, configtx.yaml) will be refactored to explicitly include all possible default configuration values.
assumptions: The text in U1 and U2 stating 'so I develop application with NodeJS' is a typo in the original requirement and actually means providing Java and Python SDKs for Hyperledger Fabric.
The development environment, CI/CD pipelines, and base Hyperledger Fabric infrastructure are already set up and functional.
Unit and integration testing efforts are included within the effort estimates for each respective activity.
Estimates represent the effort of a single mid-to-senior level software developer.
No external third-party dependencies will block the development of the specified features.

activities.activity_description: Develop a Java SDK to allow developers to build applications that interact with the Hyperledger Fabric blockchain network (U1).
Develop a Python SDK to allow developers to build applications that interact with the Hyperledger Fabric blockchain network (U2).
Implement the ability to deploy user chaincode in a pre-built form so that peers do not need to build the UCC or have the source code (U3).
Enhance VSCC validation failure logs to display the policy being used, names of signers/orgs, and lacking signatures, and propagate this info to the SDK (U4).
Set up the release process and scripts to provide downloadable platform-specific binaries for all tools including configtxgen, fabric-chaintool, and fabric-ca client (U5).
Implement the ability for a channel to independently confirm the validity of certificates issued by a Fabric CA by checking certificate fingerprints against an organization-provided list (U6).

activities.activity_name: Fabric Network Startup Tooling and Documentation
activities.activity_description: Create tools, readme files, and documentation in the fabric/test/ directory and readthedocs to provide a quick way for testers to start up a fabric blockchain network (U7).
Consolidate all default configurations into a 'config_defaults' directory and ensure all YAML files (core.yaml, orderer.yaml, configtx.yaml) contain all possible default values (U8).
